extracted.intended_audience: fiction authors preparing query materials for agents or synopses for editors/publishers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing a novel synopsis to send to literary agents or to a publisher/editor, covering purpose, structure, length, tone, and what to include or omit. Focus is on condensing a full novel into a one-to-three page plot summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to write a synopsis / necessity
rubrics_metrics.description: Only two scenarios require a synopsis: (1) when a literary agent explicitly requests a synopsis as part of query materials; (2) when you are working with a publisher or editor who specifically requests a synopsis for your next book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The synopsis is not always required; do not include one unless explicitly asked. However, it's good practice to be able to condense your story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose: synopsis versus blurb
rubrics_metrics.description: A synopsis is a detailed summary of the major events of a novel — telling the story from beginning through end — whereas a blurb is a teaser (like a movie trailer or back-cover copy) that entices readers without giving away the whole plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the synopsis to recap the entire plot so someone who never reads the novel still 'gets the gist'; use the blurb to pitch and entice readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start with the action (lead with the inciting incident)
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin the synopsis with the inciting action of the story rather than background or thematic statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Get straight to the point — open with the event that triggers the plot. Don't worry about making it flowery; clarity about the first action that sets events in motion is key. Example given: 'Starr Carter, a sixteen-year-old Black girl, attends a party in her neighborhood, Garden Heights.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't start with an overview or thematic statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not begin the synopsis with an overview sentence about the novel or its themes (e.g., 'The Hate U Give explores the effects of racism...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist talking about themes or overarching messages; the synopsis should describe plot action through beginning, middle, and end, not serve as a place for editorial or thematic discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover all major events and storylines
rubrics_metrics.description: Include all major plot events and storylines; show how events connect logically, and, if applicable, show how multiple character points of view play out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid large gaps in the story. Bridge storylines so the reader understands how each development proceeds from the previous one. If multiple POVs exist, show their arcs and how they intersect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't go into excessive detail (keep macro-level)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid minute details, sensory description, secondary-character minutiae, and long excerpts of dialogue; a synopsis should be a distilled macro-level summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omit character appearance, extraneous dialogue, and scene-by-scene description unless a specific conversation or detail directly affects plot outcomes. Keep secondary characters and subplots minimal unless they impact the main arc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give away the ending (be explicit about how the story resolves)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reveal how the novel ends; the agent or editor needs to assess the effectiveness of the ending, so do not withhold or be vague.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe closing events and the lingering emotional or thematic feeling (e.g., closure vs ambiguity). Avoid ellipses or vague phrasing; be concrete about resolution and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't provide editorial commentary or sell in the synopsis
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include evaluative or promotional language about the novel's themes, importance, or why readers will love it; the synopsis should be straightforward and 'blAND'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve selling points and thematic discussion for the query letter or verbal pitch. Example of an anti-pattern: inserting thematic analysis into the synopsis (e.g., 'Underlying the traumatic events...we see how this intergenerational cycle is difficult to break').

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and style: factual, concise, and unadorned
rubrics_metrics.description: The synopsis should be practical and plain in tone — focused on conveying plot events rather than style, flourish, or literary voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep voice neutral and summary-focused. Do not try to make the synopsis the most beautifully written piece of writing; clarity and completeness of plot matter more here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length and versions: prepare short and long synopses
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical synopsis length is one to three pages. The author recommends having two versions: a short one-page synopsis and a longer two-to-three-page synopsis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some agents request only one page; others don't specify. Having both versions ready prevents scrambling to cut content at submission time. Use the longer version to provide more detail and the one-page for tight requests.
